## Format

Every row in the Test Cases table below has **17 mandatory columns**
plus 3 metadata columns (18-20) that carry ISO 25010 / test-design
technique / API tags for the coverage gates.

### Column contract

| # | Field | Mandatory | Validation |
|---|-------|-----------|------------|
| 1 | Requirement ID | Yes | `(FR-[A-Z]+-\d+\|NFR-[A-Z]+-\d+\|BUG-\d+)`, comma-separated; every ID must resolve in `docs/SRS.md` or `qa/bugs.json` |
| 2 | Test Scenario ID | Yes | `TS-\d+` |
| 3 | Test Scenario | Yes | Human-readable scenario name (≥ 5 chars) |
| 4 | Test Case ID | Yes | `TC-[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,14}-\d+`, unique in this file |
| 5 | Test Case Title | Yes | One-line summary (≥ 5 chars) |
| 6 | Precondition | Yes | State before the test; `<br>` for multi-line |
| 7 | Test Steps | Yes | Numbered list, `<br>` between steps |
| 8 | Test Data | Yes | `key: value` pairs, `<br>` between; use `—` if none |
| 9 | Expected Result | Yes | What SHOULD happen |
| 10 | Actual Result | Auto | What DID happen (post-run writer fills this) |
| 11 | Status | Enum | `Passed \| Failed \| Blocked \| Skipped \| Pending` |
| 12 | Severity | Enum | `Critical \| High \| Medium \| Low` |
| 13 | Priority | Enum | `P1 \| P2 \| P3 \| P4` |
| 14 | Automation | Enum | `Automated \| Manual \| Semi-automated` |
| 15 | Executed By | Auto | Name from `AGENTS.md#current_user_name` |
| 16 | Execution Date | Auto | ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| 17 | Remarks/Bug ID | Conditional | If Status=Failed, MUST contain `BUG-\d+` referencing `qa/bugs.json` |
| 18 | iso25010 | Yes | Comma-separated: `FUN \| PER \| COM \| INT \| REL \| SEC \| MAI \| FLE` |
| 19 | techniques | Yes | Comma-separated: `BVA \| EQ \| DT \| STT \| PAIRWISE \| ERROR_GUESS \| UC \| RBT \| EXPLORATORY \| CHECKLIST` |
| 20 | api | If applicable | `METHOD /path` matching `docs/api.md` |

### Placement rationale

**Requirement ID sits first** — before Test Scenario, Test Case, or
anything else. This mirrors the audit sequence: *what requirement
drives this scenario → what specific case verifies it*. It's the
first field a reviewer or auditor scans, and it's the field the
FCX-SEC-PROC-001 §8.29 sign-off gate depends on.

### Auto-populated columns

Columns **10 (Actual Result), 11 (Status), 15 (Executed By), 16
(Execution Date), 17 (Remarks/Bug ID)** are filled by
`qa-testcase-result-writer.sh` after every test-runner command. Human
edits to these columns are overwritten on the next run — put narrative
notes in a separate `## Notes` section below the table if needed.

---

## Hard-block enforcement

Two gates fire on every test-runner command (`playwright test`,
`maestro test`, `pytest qa/`, `bun test`, `curl` under `qa/scripts/`,
`bash scripts/qa-retest.sh`, `/qa-signoff`, …):

1. **`qa-testcase-tracker-required.sh` (v7.9.121)** — refuses to run
   unless this file exists AND every row's mandatory cells are filled
   AND every Requirement ID resolves in `docs/SRS.md` or `qa/bugs.json`.
2. **`qa-testcase-doc-fresh-gate.sh` (v7.9.121)** — refuses to run
   when the previous run's results didn't land in this file (staleness
   detection via mtime).

**No env-var bypass by design.** To unblock, either add the missing
rows, fix the Requirement IDs, or run
`bash qa/scripts/refresh-testcases.sh` to sync last run's results.
